name.description: Friendly name for the webhook (e.g. "CF Pages deploy hook")

url.description: Target URL — POSTed on subscribed events

events.description: Subscribed event names. Empty array = all events fire this webhook. Known events: `listing.created`, `listing.updated`, `listing.deleted` — fired on writes via either admin or public API; `submission.received` — an anonymous suggestion or feedback item needs review. Fired ONLY for items that reach `pending`; spam (honeypot or failed Turnstile) is stored silently and never notifies, so the channel stays worth reading. Payload: `{ submissionId, kind, listingId }`; `review.received` — a public review is waiting for moderation. Like `submission.received`, fired ONLY for items that reach `pending`. Payload: `{ reviewId, listingId, rating }`; `review.approved` — a review was published and the listing's rating average moved. Consumers that render ratings from a build-time export need this one to know to rebuild. Payload: `{ reviewId, listingId, rating }`; `review.rejected` — a review that WAS published is no longer public, because it was unpublished, rejected or filed as spam. The mirror of `review.approved`, and the more urgent of the pair: it is what a consumer rebuilds on to take defamatory or abusive text off their site. Fired ONLY on the `approved` -> not-approved transition — rejecting a pending review was never public and fires nothing. Payload: `{ reviewId, listingId, rating }`; `comment.received` — a page comment is waiting for moderation. Fired ONLY for items that reach `pending`. Payload: `{ commentId, path }`; `comment.approved` — a page comment was published. A static site that renders comments rebuilds on this. Payload: `{ commentId, path }`; `comment.rejected` — a page comment that WAS published is no longer public (rejected, unpublished or filed as spam). Fired ONLY on the `approved` -> not-approved transition; subscribe to it if you render comments, since it is what takes one down. Payload: `{ commentId, path }`; `comment.updated` — the editors' reply on a currently-approved comment was set, changed or cleared. Not fired for replies on unpublished comments. Payload: `{ commentId, path }`; `listing.boosted` — a listing became a premium listing, by purchase or by an operator grant. Payload: `{ listingId, paymentId?, amountCents?, currency? }`. A `listing.updated` is ALWAYS fired alongside it, so a consumer already subscribed to that will rebuild without subscribing to this one; subscribe to this if you want to treat a boost specially. `test.ping` — only fired from the test endpoint, bypasses debounce. Unknown names are REJECTED with 400. They used to be accepted for forward-compat, but a typo then produced a webhook that looked healthy and never fired — subscribe to a new event once it exists.

secret.description: Shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 payload signing. When set, every dispatch includes an `X-ED-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header — verify on your end by computing HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using this secret. Verify each ATTEMPT on its own bytes: a retry re-serialises the body with a fresh `timestamp`, so the signature legitimately differs between attempts of the same delivery. To deduplicate, use `X-ED-Delivery-Id`, which is stable across all attempts — see §13 of the integrator changelog. If unset, no signature header is sent (delivery still works). Write-only: no endpoint ever returns it, not even the create response. Responses carry `hasSecret: true|false` instead. Store your copy at the point you generate it — if you lose it, PATCH a new one rather than expecting to read the old one back.

debounceMs.description: Debounce window in milliseconds. Multiple events within the window collapse to a single dispatch — useful for collapsing bulk imports into one rebuild. NULL inherits the global default (30 000ms / 30s). Range: 0 (no debounce) to 600 000 (10 minutes) — the full range is honoured, including values ABOVE the global default, which used to be silently capped. When multiple webhooks for a directory specify different values, the smallest wins for the directory as a whole; webhooks leaving it NULL express no preference and do not drag the others down — v1 limitation.
